en: The Mahāpratihāryasūtra: The Blessed Buddha was staying at Rājagṛha in the Bamboo Grove, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place;

he was honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, brahmins, householders, merchants, country folk, wealthy men, guild-leaders, and caravan leaders—and the Blessed One received [offerings of] robes...

The requisites of alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal provisions for the sick were not honored, revered, esteemed, or worshipped by kings, royal ministers, brahmins, householders, merchants, countryfolk,
wealthy men, guild-leaders, and caravan-chiefs; nor did they receive [offerings of] robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal provisions for the sick.
[regarding] the medicinal requisites;
then it occurred to Māra, the Evil One: "For a long time I have harassed the ascetic Gautama, yet I have not found an opportunity. What if I were to harass the heretics as well?"
At that time, six teachers, beginning with Pūraṇa— though they were not omniscient— dwelt in dependence upon Rājagṛha while conceiving the pride of being omniscient.
Then Māra, the Evil One, having transformed himself into the likeness of Pūraṇa, approached Maskarī.
Gośālīputra approached him; having approached, he began to display before Maskarin Gośālīputra the miracles of blazing, heating, raining, and flashing lightning. Maskarin Gośālīputra said:
"Pūraṇa, have you attained such a multitude of qualities? [He replied: "I have attained them."

Thus, in the presence of Sañjayin Vairaṭṭīputra, Ajita Keśakambala, Kakuda Kātyāyana, and the Nirgrantha Jñātiputra, he began to display the miracles of blazing, heating, raining, and flashing lightning. Pūraṇa also said: "Such a multitude of virtues as these have been [attained] by you."
"Attained! Attained!
Thus, having fashioned himself in the likeness of Maskarin Gośālīputra, he approached everyone as before, saying: "Such multitudes of qualities have been attained by you—attained!"

In this way, having transformed himself into the likeness of Sañjayin Vairaṭṭīputra, he approached them all, as before. [In this way, having transformed himself into the likeness of Ajita Keśakambalin, he approached them all, as before. In this way, [having transformed himself into the likeness] of Kakuda Kātyāyana...
Having manifested himself in the likeness of Nigaṇṭha Jñātiputra, he approached all of them as before. In this way, having manifested himself in the likeness of Nigaṇṭha Jñātiputra,
he approached all of them as before.
Each one of them reflected: "All of these are not possessed of great supernatural power (*ṛddhi*) and great majesty (*mahānubhāva*), with the single exception of myself.
Then, at another time, [the six teachers], Pūraṇa and the others, gathered in the hall of disputation.
When the six had gathered together, this kind of conversation arose among them:
"In former times, we were honored by you; we were treated with respect, saluted, revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, brahmins, householders, and merchants."

We were formerly recipients of the requisites— robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal provisions for the sick— from the wealthy people of the countryside, the guild-leaders, and the caravan-merchants; yet now we are neither honored nor revered, and as before, we are no longer recipients of robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal provisions for the sick.

[He is provided] with the requisites of medicine for the sick. But, venerable sirs, this ascetic Gautama is honored, revered, [and respected], as before, up until: the ascetic Gautama is a recipient of the requisites of robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicines for the sick.

"O sirs, we shall challenge the ascetic Gautama to a display of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) regarding a state superior to that of ordinary men. If the ascetic Gautama demonstrates one such supernatural feat, we shall demonstrate two; if the ascetic Gautama demonstrates two, we shall demonstrate four. If the ascetic Gautama [demonstrates] four...

“Maṇo Gautama has eight followers; we have sixteen. Śramaṇa Gautama has sixteen; we have thirty-two. In this way, they said, “As long as the śramaṇa Gautama displays a miracle of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) regarding a superhuman state (*uttaramanuṣyadharma*), we shall display twice that, thrice that, [and so on] regarding superhuman states.”

Then the six teachers, Pūraṇa and the others, approached King Bimbisāra. Having approached, they greeted King Bimbisāra with wishes for victory and long life, and said this: "O King, we are possessed of supernatural powers and proclaimers of knowledge; the ascetic Gautama is also [possessed of] supernatural power..."

The one who professes knowledge considers himself to be a proponent of knowledge. Therefore, it is fitting for the proponent of knowledge to display a miracle of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) regarding a superhuman state (*uttaramanuṣyadharma*) together with the proponent of knowledge. If the ascetic Gautama displays one miracle of supernatural power regarding a superhuman state, we shall display two; if two, [we shall display] two as before.

"Let us display a miracle of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) that surpasses human capacity by twofold and threefold; let the ascetic Gautama come halfway along the road, and we too shall go halfway."

Then the six teachers, Pūraṇa and the others, approached King Prasenajit of Kosala. Having approached him and greeted King Prasenajit of Kosala with wishes for victory and long life, they said: "O Lord, we are possessed of supernatural powers and are speakers of knowledge."

The ascetic Gautama also considers himself to be possessed of supernatural power and a proclaimer of knowledge. Therefore, it is fitting that a proclaimer of knowledge should display a higher human feat of supernatural power alongside another proclaimer of knowledge;
if the ascetic Gautama displays even one higher human feat of supernatural power, [I shall display two].
"We are two; Śramaṇa Gautama is two. We are four; Śramaṇa Gautama is four.
We are eight; Śramaṇa Gautama is eight. We are sixteen; Śramaṇa Gautama is sixteen.
We are thirty-two," and so on, until Śramaṇa Gautama [attained] supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) regarding a state superior to that of human beings.
"He will display a miraculous feat; we shall display one twice as great, or even three times as great, a superhuman feat of supernatural power. Let the ascetic Gautama come halfway along the road;
we too shall go halfway along the road."
King Prasenajit of Kośala said: "Sirs, if that is so, wait for a moment while I consult the Blessed One. They replied: "Your Majesty, very well; let it be so, we shall wait."
Then King Prasenajit of Kośala approached the Blessed One.

Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Prasenajit of Kośala said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, these heretics [challenge] the Blessed One regarding what is superhuman..."

They challenge [us] regarding the Dharma through the miracle of supernatural power (*ṛddhi-prātihārya*). Therefore, may the Blessed One display a supernatural power beyond the human realm (*uttare-manuṣya-dharme ṛddhi-prātihāryam*) in order to rebuke the heretics, to gladden the gods and humans, and to delight the hearts of the virtuous.

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to King Prasenajit of Kosala: "Great King, I do not teach the Dharma to my disciples in this way: 'O monks, you must display the miracle of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*)—that which transcends the human condition—to every Brahmin and householder who comes to you.'"
"Nevertheless, I teach the Dharma to my disciples thus: 'O monks, dwell with your virtues concealed and your evils revealed.
A second and even a third time, King Prasenajit Kauśala said this to the Blessed One: 'These..."
"Venerable Sir, the non-Buddhist teachers challenge the Blessed One to a contest of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) regarding a state superior to that of ordinary humans.

Therefore, may the Blessed One display a supernatural power regarding a state superior to that of ordinary humans, in order to rebuke the non-Buddhist teachers, to gladden [the assembly], to satisfy gods and humans, and to delight the hearts of the virtuous. For a second and even a third time, the Blessed One [addressed] the king...

He said this to Prasenajit, the Kosalan: "Great King, I shall not teach the Dharma to my disciples in this way: 'O monks, whenever Brahmins and householders arrive, you must display to them a superhuman feat of supernatural power (ṛddhiprātihārya). Rather, I teach the Dharma to my disciples in this manner:"
"I teach: 'O monks, dwell concealing your virtues and revealing your faults.
"Sirs, whether the ascetic Gautama flees or seeks out an ally, how should we proceed in this matter? This thought occurred to them: "Sirs..."
"Certainly, the ascetic Gautama is seeking an ally; if it is your wish, we too shall seek an ally.
Now at that time, in Kuśinagarī, there lived a wandering mendicant named Subhadra who was old and decrepit.

There was an old man, an elder among the Mallas of Kuśinagara, who was honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped [as one equal to an Arhat]. Having made a secret agreement, they approached him and said:
"Subhadra, you have been our fellow-practitioner; we shall [challenge] the ascetic Gautama on the matter of higher knowledge."
He was challenged by means of a miracle of supernatural power regarding a superhuman state; [they] provided assistance. They said:

"Sirs, you have not done well in that the ascetic Gautama has been challenged to a miracle of supernatural power regarding a superhuman state. For what reason? Because he possesses great supernatural power and great majesty."
How is this known? From logical inference. What is the inference here?

Venerable sir, when the ascetic Gautama had not yet appeared in the world, I used to spend my daytime rest on the bank of the Mandākinī lotus pond. Then, having taken my alms-food, I would go to the great lake Anavatapta.

...to enjoy [it]. There, the deities dwelling in Anavatapta, while I am seated in a secluded place, draw up water and offer it to me. When the ascetic Gautama appeared in the world, his foremost disciple was named Śāriputra, and he had a novice monk named Cunda. Taking a rag-robe (*pāṃsukūla*), he—

It goes to the great lake Anavatapta; the deities dwelling there at Anavatapta wash that rag-robe (*pāṃsukūla*) and offer it to him. With that washing-water they sprinkle themselves. He, with whom even we—along with our disciples and grand-disciples—are not equal—he has attained supernatural power (*ṛddhi*) regarding the higher human state (*uttare manuṣyadharma*). You [should know] him...
"Having been invited by the noble one, we have not acted rightly," they said to one another. "Sirs, even he belongs to that same faction. Let us go;
let us search for someone else. Having honored him with hypocritical conduct, they departed.
Standing in a certain secluded spot on the earth, they engage in conversation.
"A man possessing the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijña*) dwells there; let us go to him, for he will provide us with assistance. [Thus they spoke] to another.
"He will provide us with assistance.
Now at that time, in a certain cave of the Himalayas, [there was] various...

About five hundred sages dwell there; most of them possess the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*). From among them, one who possessed the five superknowledges went down to the vicinity of a village. He...
He related exactly what had occurred; they, having become joyful, approached him, and then, having become joyful toward one another, [they departed].

"Sirs, you shall be our fellow-students; we have summoned the ascetic Gautama with a display of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) regarding a superhuman state (*uttaramanuṣyadharma*), so please provide us with assistance. They replied, "Sirs..."
They departed;
meanwhile, King Prasenajit of Kosala had a half-brother named Kāla, who was a prince of the same lineage.
It was thrown and fell upon his shoulder. It was seen by others—the world consisting of friends, enemies, and neutrals—and they informed the ministers; the ministers, too, [informed the king].
He gave them this command: "Go, sirs; Prince Kāla has been abandoned by me; let him be made one with impaired hands and feet."

He remained there surrounded by a great multitude of people. When the heretics passed through that place, they were addressed by his kinsmen: "Noble ones, [here are] the limbs and members of Prince Kāla; [behold] this truthful invocation!"
When the Venerable Ānanda arrived at that place while wandering for alms, he was addressed by them: "Noble one, [here are] the limbs and members of Prince Kāla, [obtained] through a vow of truth."
[He] addressed the young man Uttara: "Come, young man, go to where the Blessed One is.

Having approached, bow your head at the feet of the Blessed One in our name, and inquire after his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, vigor, strength, well-being, and blamelessness."
"And [inform him] of his dwelling in comfort, and speak thus: 'Venerable sir, here the non-Buddhist teachers are seated together, assembled;

now, if the Blessed One deems it the right time. " "So be it, Your Majesty," replied the young brahmin Uttara to King Prasenajit of Kośala, and having assented, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he...
Having exchanged various greetings and pleasantries with the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
As he was seated to one side, the young brahmin Uttara said this to the Blessed One: "O sir, the king..."

"Gautama, Prasenajit of Kosala bows his head at the feet of the Blessed Gautama and inquires after his freedom from affliction, freedom from illness, ease of movement, vigor, strength, well-being, blamelessness, and his dwelling in comfort. May King Prasenajit of Kosala and you both be happy. [The King said: "So be it."
"O Gautama, Prasenajit of Kośala says this: 'The heretics are seated and assembled in the pavilion of miracles; now, Blessed One, do as you deem the time has come.
The Blessed One said: 'Go, Uttara. The young brahmin Uttara, thinking 'I have arrived today,' set out."

Empowered by the Blessed One in such a way that he rose into the expanse of the sky like a king of swans with outspread wings, he was beheld by many hundreds of thousands of living beings whose eyes were wide with wonder due to his shouts of "kilikilā" and other cries;
thus being gazed upon, he descended through the air into the pavilion of miracles. Having seen that splendor, [he...]

King Prasenajit of Kośala, his mind overcome with wonder, said this to the non-Buddhist ascetics: "Venerable sirs, the Blessed One has displayed a miracle of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*) that transcends human conditions. Now the turn has come for you; you should display one. They replied: "Your Majesty, there is a great crowd of people here."
They had assembled; wait, for who knows whose miraculous power this is—whether that of the ascetic Gautama or ours?
Immediately thereafter, by means of his supernatural power, Gaṇḍaka Ārāmaka [brought] mountains from Mount Gandhamādana...
Spread with branches and twigs, adorned with pale fruit, and frequented by many flocks of birds.
